evals.prompt: My Hibiki effect prints the total once but never again after I do `cart.items << item`. Why?
evals.expected_output: Explains that in-place mutation is not a write (the state still holds the same object, so `==` sees no change), and shows the fix: assign a fresh array (`cart.items = cart.items + [item]` or `update { it + [item] }`), or `equals: false` as the escape hatch.
expectations: Explains that `<<` mutates the array in place and never goes through the signal's writer, so no subscriber is notified
Recommends assigning a fresh array (`+= [item]`, `+`, `[*items, item]`, `update { it + [item] }`) as the primary fix
Warns that assigning the same (mutated) object back is also dropped because it is `==` to itself
Mentions `equals: false` as the escape hatch that makes a self-assignment notify
Mentions the positional-vs-block default trap for `Hibiki::Reactive` (`state(:items) { [] }`)

Every code sample uses real entry points (`Hibiki::State.new`, `Hibiki::Effect.new`, `include Hibiki::DSL` + `state`/`effect`, or `Hibiki::Reactive` macros); no invented module methods such as `Hibiki.effect`

evals.prompt: Write a Ruby class with hibiki that tracks a temperature and only logs when it changes by more than 0.5 degrees.
evals.expected_output: A class including Hibiki::Reactive (or plain signals) with `state :temperature, ..., equals: ->(prev, nxt) { (prev - nxt).abs <= 0.5 }` and an `effect { puts ... }`; explains that the comparator returning truthy means unchanged, and that the effect runs once at creation.
expectations: Uses the `equals:` option with a callable comparator taking (prev, next) rather than hand-rolled diffing in the effect
The comparator returns truthy when the difference is within 0.5 (treated as unchanged) and falsy otherwise
The logging is an `effect` (or Reactive `effect { }`), not a manual method call after each write
Notes that the effect runs once at creation (first log at construction)
Uses correct hibiki API spellings (`Hibiki::State.new(v, equals:)` / `state :temp, v, equals:` / `include Hibiki::Reactive`)
Saved thermometer.rb runs under `ruby -I lib` and logs exactly three times for the sequence 20.0, 20.3, 20.5, 20.6, 20.2, 19.9 (at 20.0, 20.6, 19.9)

evals.prompt: I'm using hibiki signals from a Sidekiq job and a Puma thread and getting weird results — is it thread safe?
evals.expected_output: Explains confinement, not locking: a graph belongs to one thread, other threads send it messages (Queue or actor pattern) rather than writing signals directly; tracking window is per fiber and inherited, batch state is per thread and not inherited; one world per Ractor.
expectations: States that signals hold no locks and a graph belongs to one thread (confinement, not locking)
Recommends sending writes from other threads to the owner thread via a Queue or actor pattern rather than writing signals directly
Mentions that tracking state is per fiber and inherited while batch state is per thread and not inherited by new fibers
Mentions that each Ractor has an independent reactive world
Does not claim hibiki is thread-safe for concurrent writes
Points out that Sidekiq and Puma are normally separate processes, so a signal graph in one is invisible to the other and the fix is cross-process messaging (DB, Redis, broadcast), not locking
